title: Bash startup files
subtitle: Login vs non-login — which files run and how to source them

cards.meaning: Reads /etc/profile, then the first readable of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile
cards.notes: Only one of the three personal files is read — first existing readable wins. On logout: ~/.bash_logout.

cards.example: Terminal opened from a desktop icon/menu
cards.notes: /etc/profile and the ~/.bash_profile trio are not read. Memory hook: non-login = rc only.

cards.meaning: Start a login shell as you (read profile files) — does not become root
cards.notes: Same UID, no password. Use to test /etc/profile and ~/.bash_profile without a new SSH.

cards.meaning: Switch to root (or another user) — not a startup-file switch
cards.notes: Needs root’s (or that user’s) password. Changes UID. Job is substitute user, not “start a login shell as me.”

cards.meaning: Switch to root with root’s clean login environment
cards.notes: Still becomes root (or that user). The - only gives their home/PATH — not “the other way to start your login shell.”

cards.meaning: Runs when an interactive login shell exits
cards.notes: Per-user. Only for that login shell’s exit — not every terminal close.
Typical line in ~/.bash_profile so login shells get aliases too. Space required after the dot.

cards.meaning: Same as . — read and run the file here (Bash-specific)
cards.notes: Not required by POSIX; dash/sh may say “source: not found.” Prefer . in portable profiles.

cards.meaning: Print current shell name; leading - often means login
cards.notes: -bash (or -su) is a common login-shell clue. Pair with shopt login_shell.

cards.meaning: Print on/off — is this a login shell?
cards.notes: Definitive check while studying. on = login path; off = typically ~/.bashrc only if interactive.

cards.meaning: Tried in that order; only the first readable one is used
cards.example: If ~/.bash_profile exists, the other two are skipped
cards.notes: Memory hook: login = profile family. System first (/etc/profile), then one personal file.
